reasoning_content: The goal is an equivalence between two statements about `∀ᶠ` in an ultrafilter `f`. The left-hand side is `∀ᶠ x in f, p x → q x`. The right-hand side is `(∀ᶠ x in f, p x) → ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`. We can rewrite the implication `p x → q x` using `imp_iff_not_or` to `¬ p x ∨ q x`. This transforms the left-hand side into `∀ᶠ x in f, ¬ p x ∨ q x`. Then we apply `Ultrafilter.eventually_or` to split this into `(∀ᶠ x in f, ¬ p x) ∨ ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`. Next, we rewrite `∀ᶠ x in f, ¬ p x` using `Ultrafilter.eventually_not` to `¬ ∀ᶠ x in f, p x`. The goal becomes `(¬ ∀ᶠ x in f, p x) ∨ ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`. Finally, we rewrite this disjunction back into an implication using `imp_iff_not_or` again, but in reverse, to get `(∀ᶠ x in f, p x) → ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`, which matches the right-hand side. The `simp_rw` tactic applies these rewrites in sequence, using the three lemmas provided.

The right-hand side is an implication between two eventual statements. The left-hand side can be transformed using `imp_iff_not_or`, which rewrites `p x → q x` as `¬ p x ∨ q x`. This yields `∀ᶠ x in f, ¬ p x ∨ q x`. Then `Ultrafilter.eventually_or` allows splitting this into a disjunction of two eventual statements: `(∀ᶠ x in f, ¬ p x) ∨ ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`. Next, `Ultrafilter.eventually_not` rewrites `∀ᶠ x in f, ¬ p x` as `¬∀ᶠ x in f, p x`. So the left-hand side becomes `¬∀ᶠ x in f, p x ∨ ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`. The right-hand side of the original goal is `(∀ᶠ x in f, p x) → ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`, which by `imp_iff_not_or` is equivalent to `¬∀ᶠ x in f, p x ∨ ∀ᶠ x in f, q x`. Thus both sides reduce to the same disjunction after applying these three lemmas. The `simp` tactic with these three lemmas will rewrite both sides to the same expression, closing the goal.

Therefore, both sides become identical after these rewrites. The `simp_rw` tactic applies these three rewrites in sequence, transforming the entire goal into a trivial equivalence.
